question: What do the passages conclude about sleep duration and next-day attention test scores in the summarized student samples?
required_claim: Shorter sleep is linked to lower attention scores on average; one study finds the link depends on caffeine use.

passages.text: A landscaping crew planted new shrubs outside the admin building.
Study Sleep-A (n=150) reported that students sleeping under six hours had lower next-day attention test scores than peers sleeping seven to eight hours.
The career fair reserved Booth 12 for nonprofit employers.
A packaging label printer jammed twice during orientation week.
Study Sleep-B found no reliable sleep–attention association among students who consumed more than two caffeinated drinks before testing.
The theater society postponed auditions by one day due to a room conflict.
A recycling drive collected cardboard outside the dining hall.
